claims.text: Optimized thermomechanical processing of near-equiatomic NiTi can reproducibly tune its temperature-dependent plastic deformation behavior.
Thermomechanical processing can shift the martensitic transformation range of NiTi.
Thermomechanical processing can refine phase-boundary morphology in NiTi.
Near-equiatomic NiTi shape-memory alloy contains martensitic and austenitic phases.
Controlled aging and cooling cycles can adjust the transformation temperature of NiTi.
Controlled aging and cooling cycles can refine phase-boundary features in NiTi.
Thermomechanical processing produces modified phase-boundary morphology in NiTi.
Thermomechanical processing produces an optimized grain structure in NiTi.
The processing intervention alters the relative stability of martensite and austenite in NiTi.
The processing intervention alters the volume fractions of martensite and austenite in NiTi.
Changes in martensite and austenite stability and volume fraction modulate dislocation mobility.
Changes in dislocation mobility modulate the plastic deformation behavior of NiTi as temperature changes.
Treated NiTi will exhibit a measurable change in yield strength relative to untreated NiTi.
Treated NiTi will exhibit changed deformation modes relative to untreated NiTi.
Treatment may enhance pseudoelasticity or superelasticity in the temperature regime dominated by phase transformation.
The proposed response is limited to compositions close to equiatomic NiTi and processing conditions that do not substantially alter bulk chemistry.
Composition deviations or extreme processing conditions may prevent the predicted deformation response.
